title: MC 26.x is unobfuscated, no Yarn
body: yarn/26.x endpoints return empty, intermediary is 0.0.0 placeholder. Use loom 1.16.2 + plugin id net.fabricmc.fabric-loom + Mojang official names (mojmap). Verified 2026-10-04 via meta.fabricmc.net.

title: Loom/Gradle/JDK matrix for 26.2
body: loom 1.16.2 requires Gradle 9.4+ and JDK 25 (Gradle 8.14 cannot run on JDK 25: major version 69). Fabric API 0.161.0+26.2, loader 0.19.5. Non-obfuscated pipeline uses plain implementation deps, no mappings line, no modImplementation.

title: Never resolve key display names before window exists
body: KeyMapping.getTranslatedKeyMessage/getDisplayName calls native glfwGetKeyName via memoized supplier. Called pre-window it queues GLFW 0x10001 which crashes later inside GLX._initGlfw with no mod frames in the stack. Log raw key codes at init instead. Proven by bisection 2026-10-04.

title: 26.x GUI/input API names
body: DrawContext->GuiGraphicsExtractor(text/fill/enableScissor/pose), Screen.render->extractRenderState, TextFieldWidget->EditBox, KeyBinding->KeyMapping(isDown/consumeClick/setKey/resetMapping), Screen.currentScreen->Gui.screen(), hudHidden->Gui.hud.isHidden(), TextRenderer->Font(width/lineHeight), Text->Component, Identifier stays (of->fromNamespaceAndPath).

title: Windows @TempDir cleanup flakes
body: JUnit @TempDir deletion can fail on Windows file locks (Failed to close extension context) with zero test failures. Rerun once before blaming code; treat as environment flake.

title: Bisect startup crashes, don't guess
body: Empty entrypoint -> title screen proves jar presence is harmless. Minimal init -> pieces. The breaking piece here was one debug log line resolving a key display name (native call pre-window). Experiments beat theories.

title: Always override hashCode with equals
body: Equal objects must have equal hash codes (Object contract). Break it and HashMap/HashSet silently lose entries. IDE-generate both or use records.

title: Prefer try-with-resources over manual close
body: try (var in = open(...)) closes even on exception and suppresses correctly. Manual close in finally leaks on early throws and hides the real exception.

title: Optional is not for fields or parameters
body: Optional is a return-type hint for 'maybe absent'. Fields/params with Optional add allocation + NPE-equivalents; overloads or null-objects are clearer.

title: ArrayList beats LinkedList almost always
body: LinkedList has per-node allocation + pointer chasing; ArrayList wins iteration, index access and usually insertion. Use ArrayDeque for queues/stacks.

title: ConcurrentHashMap: no nulls, atomic helpers
body: CHM forbids null keys/values (fail-fast by design). Use computeIfAbsent/merge for atomic updates instead of get-then-put races.

title: Stream pitfalls: reuse and side effects
body: A stream is single-use (reuse throws IllegalStateException). Avoid mutating external state in forEach — prefer collectors; parallel() only for CPU-heavy stateless pipelines.

title: records for dumb data carriers
body: record Point(int x, int y) gives equals/hashCode/toString + immutability free. Validate in compact constructor. Not for mutable entities or inheritance.

title: Java 21 is LTS; target release explicitly
body: Set maven.compiler.release or Gradle toolchain languageVersion so code compiles against the right API, not just the running JDK. LTS = long support window.

title: plugin.yml minimum that boots
body: Paper needs name, version, main (full class path) and api-version (e.g. 1.21). Missing/wrong main = InvalidPluginException before any of your code runs.

title: Events: Listener + registerEvents, never forget
body: A method with @EventHandler does nothing until getServer().getPluginManager().registerEvents(listener, plugin). Most common 'my event never fires' cause.

title: Scheduler: never touch Bukkit API async
body: runTaskAsynchronously is for IO/compute only. World, entities, inventories must be touched on the main thread (runTask / runTaskLater). Violations corrupt worlds silently.

title: saveDefaultConfig before getConfig reads
body: Ship config.yml defaults in the jar and call saveDefaultConfig() in onEnable, otherwise fresh installs read an empty config and every get returns defaults/zeroes.

title: Permissions: declare with sane defaults
body: Declare each permission in plugin.yml with default op/true/false and description. Checking undeclared nodes works but is invisible to admins and LuckPerms UIs.

title: MiniMessage over legacy section codes
body: Adventure MiniMessage (<red>, <bold>, <click:>) replaces error-prone &/§ codes and prevents broken color bleed. Never mix both in one string.

title: PersistentDataContainer for custom item data
body: Store plugin data via itemMeta.getPersistentDataContainer().set(new NamespacedKey(plugin, 'k'), PersistentDataType.STRING, v). Survives restarts; display names/lore do not.

title: Commands: executor + tab-completer + permission
body: Register in plugin.yml (name, usage, permission), setExecutor + setTabCompleter in onEnable. Always null-check args length before args[0] (ArrayIndexOutOfBounds is the #1 plugin crash).

title: Always commit the Gradle wrapper
body: gradlew + gradle/wrapper/ pin the exact Gradle version. 'Works on my machine' build failures are 90% wrapper-vs-system Gradle mismatches. Never require a system Gradle.

title: implementation vs compileOnly vs runtimeOnly
body: implementation = compile+runtime, compileOnly = provided at runtime (server APIs like paper-api), runtimeOnly = drivers. Wrong scope = NoClassDefFoundError in production only.

title: Repositories first, mavenCentral covers most
body: Declare repositories { mavenCentral() } plus paper-repo for Paper API. A missing repository gives 'could not resolve' — read WHICH repo was searched before blaming the artifact.

title: Gradle daemon and --offline for speed
body: Keep the daemon on (default) — cold JVM startup dominates small builds. --offline reuses cache on planes/trains; --refresh-dependencies only when artifacts actually changed.

title: Version catalogs beat scattered strings
body: Centralize in gradle/libs.versions.toml (versions, libraries, plugins). One place to bump, Dependabot-friendly, no more 'which subproject pins old junit'.

title: Shade only what you must, relocate the rest
body: Shading full libraries without relocation breaks other plugins (class clashes). Relocate (shadowJar relocate) or depend on server-provided APIs instead.

title: assertThrows instead of try-fail
body: assertThrows(InvalidPluginException.class, () -> load(bad)) documents the contract in one line. try{...fail()} hides which line threw and swallows assertion errors.

title: Parameterized tests kill copy-paste cases
body: @ParameterizedTest + @ValueSource/@CsvSource runs one body over many inputs. 20 near-identical @Tests = 20 places to diverge; one parameterized = one truth.

title: Mockito: mock roles, not values
body: Mock boundaries (clock, http, db), not data holders. when(...).thenReturn for queries, verify() for commands. Mocking everything = testing nothing.

title: One behavior per test, name it
body: test_code_review_finds_debt beats test_review2. When it fails at 3am the name must explain the broken contract without opening the file.

title: Fixture builders over giant setup blocks
body: A 40-line @BeforeEach hides what each test needs. Tiny builders (pluginWith(name)) keep each test readable and independent.

title: Flaky first, guilty later
body: A test failing once on Windows file locks or timing is environment until proven otherwise: rerun isolated, then quarantine with a reason, never silently delete.

title: venv per project, never system pip
body: python -m venv .venv isolates deps. System-wide installs collide versions between projects and break unrelated tools on upgrade.

title: pytest fixtures over setup/teardown soup
body: tmp_path, monkeypatch and small custom fixtures compose; setUp/tearDown ordering gets fragile past 3 concerns. -q for signal, -x to stop at first failure.

title: GIL: threads for IO, processes for CPU
body: Threads overlap network/disk waits but not CPU crunching (GIL). CPU-bound parallelism = multiprocessing or native extensions releasing the GIL.

title: pathlib over string paths
body: Path / 'sub' / 'f' is cross-platform and readable; os.path.join chains + manual separators break on Windows. resolve() before comparing locations.

title: Editable installs for local tooling
body: pip install -e . makes `import mypkg` track the working tree — no reinstall after every edit, no stale-copy mysteries in tests.

title: Never rebase public history
body: Rebase rewrites commits others may have pulled. Rule: rebase private branches, merge public ones. Pushed + shared = append-only.

title: gitignore does not untrack tracked files
body: Adding to .gitignore stops future tracking only. Already-committed files need git rm --cached first, otherwise secrets stay in history forever (then rotate them).

title: Bisect beats staring at logs
body: git bisect automates 'which commit broke it' in log2(n) steps. Mark good/bad, let it checkout, run the failing test. Guessing wastes hours.

title: Stash with -u for full context switch
body: git stash push -u includes untracked files; plain stash leaves them behind and the 'clean tree' is a lie. Name stashes (-m) or lose them.

title: Secrets never enter git
body: .env + .gitignore + env vars; committed secret = compromised secret (history never forgets). Rotate immediately if leaked, don't just delete the line.

title: Parameterize every query
body: String-built SQL with user input is injection by construction. Placeholders (?) + driver escaping, always — no 'trusted internal input' exceptions.

title: Hash passwords with bcrypt/argon2, never plain MD5/SHA
body: Fast hashes crack in hours on GPUs. Use adaptive KDFs (bcrypt, argon2, scrypt) with per-user salts; MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256 are for integrity, not passwords.

title: Dependencies are attack surface: update deliberately
body: Pin versions, review changelogs, update on schedule — not never, not blindly. Known-CVE libs cause most breaches, not zero-days.
